findings.original_line: Part~XV of \repo{foundations-and-computation/polish-models-of-omnific-arithmetic} (batch-92 manuscript~05; AI-assisted, unrefereed, not formalized) uses the same integer comparisons for field embeddings $\mathcal L^\Gamma\to\mathcal L^\Delta$ between left-finite Levi-Civita fields with real algebraic coefficients and exponent groups $0\ne\Gamma,\Delta\le\R$, where the induced value-group map is multiplication by one real $\lambda>0$ (\lbl{pma:rk:thm:scaling}), and it classifies these embeddings by triples $(\lambda,c,u)$ (\lbl{pma:rk:thm:parameters}). Those fields are complete and uncountable, not countable subfields of $\No$, so \cref{csf:q:embeddings} is not answered. Its Cantor family of closed immediate self-copies of one Polish field (\lbl{pma:rk:thm:family}) is a different object from the Cantor families of countable subfields here.
findings.finding: The cited positive-character parametrization assumes nonzero Q-subspaces of R, not arbitrary additive subgroups.
findings.counterexample_to_unrestricted_reading: For Gamma=Delta=Z, L^Z over real algebraic coefficients is the Laurent-series field. The field automorphism t->-t has leading coefficient character c(1)=-1, outside Hom(Gamma,k_{>0}^times).
findings.minimal_correction: State that both exponent groups are nonzero Q-subspaces (use <=_Q), as in PMA.

source_premises.kind: countability premise and theorem included in source read

findings.finding: The guide omits countability in its Cantor-family summary; the cited Polish/Effros theorem and its own article retain it. The field setup also inherits the Q-subspace convention.
findings.minimal_correction: Say nonzero rational vector subspaces in the setup, and for countable Gamma of infinite rational rank in the family clause.
findings.limit: No counterexample to a separately formulated uncountable extension is claimed.

independent_algebra.checked_by_hand: rho(s)=s and rho(t)-t=-1-2t is nonzero over every field; hence k(s) is a proper subfield of k(t). Forward Laurent summability does not imply an inverse.
